close_reason: Added a 'Deserialization behaviour on malformed input' rustdoc section to AlertTrigger documenting that all malformed-shape inputs (top-level non-objects, missing/non-string/wrong-string @type) land in Unknown(Value) with the input preserved, citing the RFC 8984 §4.5.2 preserve-mandate as rationale. The behavior is now discoverable from rendered docs; consumers needing stricter checks can pattern-match on the variant and inspect the carried Value. Pairs with the probe test added under .4.
description:
**Contract risk**: `AlertTrigger`'s manual `Deserialize` impl reads:

    let v = serde_json::Value::deserialize(d)?;
    let tag = v
        .get(\"@type\")
        .and_then(|t| t.as_str())
        .unwrap_or(\"\")
        .to_owned();
    match tag.as_str() {
        \"OffsetTrigger\" => { ... }
        \"AbsoluteTrigger\" => { ... }
        _ => Ok(AlertTrigger::Unknown(v)),
    }

This accepts any JSON value, not just objects. In particular:

    let null_trigger: AlertTrigger = serde_json::from_value(json!(null)).unwrap();
    // Ok(AlertTrigger::Unknown(Value::Null))

    let array_trigger: AlertTrigger = serde_json::from_value(json!([1, 2])).unwrap();
    // Ok(AlertTrigger::Unknown(Value::Array(...)))

    let int_trigger: AlertTrigger = serde_json::from_value(json!(42)).unwrap();
    // Ok(AlertTrigger::Unknown(Value::Number(42)))

    let obj_with_nonstring_at_type: AlertTrigger = serde_json::from_value(json!({
        \"@type\": 42
    })).unwrap();
    // Ok(AlertTrigger::Unknown({\"@type\":42}))  — non-string @type silently dispatched to Unknown

The public docstring on `AlertTrigger` (lib.rs lines 557–567) talks
about \"@type field on the wire selects the variant\" and \"The
`Unknown` variant preserves any unrecognised trigger type for
round-trip fidelity\" but says nothing about non-object inputs,
nor about non-string `@type` values.

**What goes wrong for callers**:
- A consumer that expects `AlertTrigger` deserialization to fail on
  obviously malformed input (a bare integer where a trigger object
  is expected) will be surprised. The Deserialize impl is silently
  permissive.
- The RFC 8984 §4.5.2 \"MUST preserve them\" requirement applies to
  unknown trigger TYPES (i.e. unknown `@type` strings on otherwise
  well-formed objects), NOT to arbitrary JSON garbage. The current
  impl conflates those two cases.
- The existing finding JMAP-mno4.4 covers the TEST gap (no tests
  for these edge cases). This bead is the DOCS gap: a caller
  reading rustdoc has no way to know that `AlertTrigger::Unknown`
  is also the dumping ground for non-object input.

**Fix shape** (additive, non-breaking — docs only):
Update the docstring on `AlertTrigger` and on the `Unknown`
variant to say explicitly:

  \"Any input whose `@type` is not `\\\"OffsetTrigger\\\"` or
  `\\\"AbsoluteTrigger\\\"` is preserved as `Unknown(Value)`,
  including inputs that are not JSON objects at all (e.g. `null`,
  arrays, numbers) and inputs where `@type` exists but is not a
  string. Consumers requiring strict shape validation should
  call `serde_json::from_value::<serde_json::Map<...>>` on the
  inner value before pattern-matching.\"

Optional follow-up: tighten the Deserialize to reject non-object
inputs with an error. That is a breaking change for callers
relying on the current permissive behaviour and should be its own
bead.
title: AlertTrigger custom Deserialize behaviour on non-object inputs (null, [], 42, "string") is undocumented in the public docstring — accepts all of them as Unknown(Value) silently
